thread:
amanda (Customer): Hey team — hitting a really annoying issue after moving our Redwood Dedicated instance into our VPC behind the corporate proxy. SSE streams (text/event-stream) frequently cut off mid-response. Client sees partial tokens and then connection closed. Happens ~10-30s into long responses. Not seeing failures with short responses.

casey (Support): thanks for the report, amanda. can you confirm whether this is only on the dedicated/private deployment and not the hosted API? also any recent network changes at your edge (load balancer, proxy)?

amanda (Customer): correct — hosted was fine. We moved to Dedicated + VPC two weeks ago. Our infra team glued an edge proxy (company-proxy v2) in front of the ingress and there are some corporate transparent proxies that inspect traffic. They said they didn't change timeouts but we did enable MTU 9000 on some internal VLANs.

casey (Support): hmmm that could be two leads: proxy buffering/idle timeouts and MTU/path-fragmentation causing packet drops. can you try a quick repro with curl to capture the raw behavior? e.g.:

```bash
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \"https://<your-dedicated-host>/v1/streams?model=...\"
```

the `-N` keeps curl from buffering. please paste the `-v` output (headers) and any partial payload. also do you have access to server side logs for the runtime? /var/log/redwood/runtime.log or similar.

amanda (Customer): ran your curl. attaching last bits: the stream emits a few events, then I get `Connection: close` from the proxy. Headers from server before closure: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, then suddenly 502 from proxy. client curl shows `recv() failed: Connection reset by peer`.

jin (Eng Infra): thanks. `Connection reset by peer` + 502 from upstream proxy suggests the proxy is deciding to close/terminate. Corporate proxies often buffer until they see a content-length or until their internal buffer fills; chunked SSE is safe but some proxies still try to buffer if they think it's not interactive. Also MTU 9000 mixed with hosts on 1500 can break path MTU discovery leading to fragmentation and intermittent resets if DF is set.

tara (SRE): capture request/response sizes and any TCP-level resets. ask amanda to run a tcpdump at the host side and also at the proxy (if possible). commands:

```bash
sudo tcpdump -i any host <client-ip> and port 443 -w /tmp/sse.pcap
# on the runtime host capture local interface as well
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/runtime-to-proxy.pcap host <proxy-ip>
```

also collect `ss -tnp` output when repro-ing to see any RSTs and `sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -n 200 --no-pager`.

amanda (Customer): ran tcpdump. I see a burst of data and then an immediate `RST` from the proxy. No TLS alerts, just TCP RST. The sizes spike to ~16KB chunks. We're using NET/HTTP chunking from the runtime.

jin (Eng Infra): 16KB chunk + RST could be PMTU + fragmentation or proxy buffer threshold. On many corporate proxies (Bluecoat, F5 ASM, older Nginx setups) they'll drop if they see unexpected large chunk sizes or a long-lived connection without recognizable verbs. A few things to test rapidly:
1) Disable proxy (if you can) and point a client directly at the ingress public IP to confirm it's proxy-related.
2) Force smaller chunks from the runtime or enable heartbeats so the proxy sees frequent small writes. Runtime config can reduce chunk size / flush frequency. Try sending a heartbeat comment `\n: keepalive\n\n` every 3s.
3) Test MTU path: `sudo ip link show`, `ip route get 8.8.8.8`, `tracepath <proxy-ip>` to see MTU along path.

casey (Support): helpful. Amanda, if you can try 1) and 2) that will isolate it. Quick workaround we've used with other customers: toggle the runtime to emit smaller chunks and add SSE `retry:` to make client reconnect easier, or use websockets (if your proxy allows WS) which some proxies handle differently.

amanda (Customer): we tried disabling the corporate proxy and streams are stable immediately. So it's definitely the proxy. Can't disable it in prod though.

jin (Eng Infra): confirmed proxy is culprit. Next steps: either tune proxy to treat `/v1/streams` as streaming (disable buffering) or change runtime to accommodate the proxy. For nginx-style proxies add:

```nginx
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_cache off;
proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection "";
chunked_transfer_encoding off; # note: some deployments need this toggled
```

corporate appliances often have similar settings. If they can't change global behavior, ask them to create an exception for the Redwood streaming host/path.

amanda (Customer): proxy team says they can't disable buffering globally. They asked if Redwood has a server-side setting to send more frequent flushes / smaller chunks.

tara (SRE): runtime has a `stream_flush_interval_ms` and `max_chunk_bytes` flags. Eng-runtime can add a per-tenant override to be conservative when a proxy is detected. I can propose a hotfix: default to 1KB flushes for Dedicated VPC customers behind proxies.

casey (Support): I'm going to open an internal P0 with eng-runtime and eng-infra. Please attach the tcpdump and the `curl -v -N` output. Also the proxy vendor/version and any appliance logs you can get. I'll include suggested configs above.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1024. Priority: P0. Owners tagged: @eng-runtime, @eng-infra, @support. Link: https://internal.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-1024

jin (Eng Infra): quick note on MTU: if the proxy or any hop is set to jumbo frames (9000) while others are 1500, Path MTU Discovery can be blocked by firewalls, causing large packets to be dropped and the sender keeps retransmitting until it times out — that might look like partial responses then reset. Use `tracepath` and `ip -s link` to confirm no blackhole. If PMTU is broken, setting `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` on the runtime host can help as a stopgap.

amanda (Customer): we ran `tracepath` to the proxy and saw MTU 1500 all the way, so not jumbo mismatch here. Proxy team found a proxy buffer limit of 12KB per request and they were dropping/closing connections when chunked writes exceeded that before an application-level flush.

casey (Support): ok that explains the 16KB spike you reported. We should implement two-pronged remediation: short-term change runtime to flush smaller chunks + heartbeat; long-term ask proxy team to whitelist streaming endpoint or raise buffer limits.

tara (SRE): JIRA ticket for runtime tweak: RUNTIME-7892. Plan: expose `min_flush_bytes` and `heartbeat_interval_ms` in tenant config, default conservative values for Dedicated. Will aim for patch in 48 hours, then config rollout.

jin (Eng Infra): eng-infra will also prepare a KB snippet for customers on nginx/F5/Bluecoat config snippets to disable buffering for SSE endpoints and note known proxy behaviors.

casey (Support): Amanda — can you confirm whether you want us to push a tenant config change to your Dedicated instance as a short-term mitigation? We can coordinate a maintenance window since it's runtime config and should be safe to flip.

amanda (Customer): yes please. low-risk, prefer that while we work with proxy team to make a permanent exception. Please proceed.

casey (Support): starting the tenant config change now. I'll set `min_flush_bytes=1024` and `heartbeat_interval_ms=3000` for your tenant id. Expect brief reconnections (~5s) as the runtime reloads.

amanda (Customer): change applied, re-tested streaming. so far stable for 45 minutes. no partial outputs. thanks all.

oncall-bot: INC-2026-1024 status changed to Investigating. Linked PR: https://stash.redwood/r/runtime/RUNTIME-7892/1234

casey (Support): followups for the ticket: attach tcpdump, curl output, proxy appliance logs, and the runtime debug logs. eng-runtime will send a minor release and we will schedule a tenant rollout. long-term we recommend customers put streaming hosts on an egress path that avoids transparent buffering proxies or apply route/ACL exceptions.

amanda (Customer): thanks — I appreciate the quick turnaround. one last Q: is there any header or metadata we could add to the requests to indicate "streaming" so proxies can auto-detect?

jin (Eng Infra): some proxies look at `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, but many still buffer. We could add a `X-Redwood-Streaming: 1` header as a suggestion for customers to program proxy rules around. I'll add that as an opt-in header in the next patch and document it in the KB.

casey (Support): summary (for ticket): root cause = corporate proxy buffering / buffer limit + chunked writes > buffer size causing RST/502. MTU not the culprit here. Remediation = short-term tenant config (smaller flushes + heartbeat) applied and working; mid-term = eng-runtime patch to expose controls and add `X-Redwood-Streaming` header; long-term = KB for proxy config exceptions.

amanda (Customer): perfect. closing on my side after monitoring for a day. will reopen if anything else crops up. really appreciate the help. :heart:

casey (Support): great — I'll move incident to Monitoring and follow up with eng-runtime for the patch ETA. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
